The database schema named 'rschema_0246' consists of five tables: User, Crew, Film_Information, Comment, and Film_Ranking.
The User table is used for storing user information. It contains five columns: Email (a string of up to 255 characters), Login_Status (a string of up to 255 characters), Password (a string of up to 255 characters), User_ID (an integer primary key), and Username (a string of up to 255 characters).
The Crew table is used for storing crew information. It contains four columns: Crew_ID (an integer primary key), Crew_Information (a string of up to 255 characters), Crew_Members (a string of up to 255 characters), and Crew_Name (a string of up to 255 characters). The Login_Status column is a boolean type.
The Film_Information table is used for storing film information. It contains four columns: Information_Content (a string of up to 255 characters), Information_ID (an integer primary key), Information_Title (a string of up to 255 characters), and Publish_Time (a datetime type).
The Comment table is used for storing comments. It contains four columns: Comment_Content (a string of up to 255 characters), Comment_Time (a datetime type), Film_ID (an integer not null), and User_ID (an integer not null). The primary key of this table is a combination of Information_ID, User_ID, and Comment_Time. It references the Film_Information and User tables via the Film_ID and User_ID columns respectively.
Finally, the Film_Ranking table is used for storing film rankings. It contains four columns: Film_ID (an integer not null), Ranking_ID (an integer primary key), Ranking_Position (a string of up to 255 characters), and Update_Time (a datetime type). This table references the Film_Information table via the Film_ID column.
All columns allow null values except for the Film_ID, User_ID, and Information_ID in the Comment table. The primary keys are unique and auto-incremented. The foreign key constraints ensure referential integrity, i.e., the relationships between tables are maintained.

System Requirements Function Description

1. Front-end Function
Film and TV Information Browsing: Users can browse the latest movie and TV series information
Film and TV Reviews: Users can comment on movies and TV series
Film and TV Sharing: Users can share their favorite movies and TV series
Film and TV Rankings: Users can view the most popular movie and TV series rankings
Film and TV Search: Users can search for movies and TV series of interest by keywords
Crew Information Query: Users can query the crew information of movies and TV series, such as directors, actors, etc.
User Login: Users can register and log in to the website to enjoy more personalized services
Crew Login: Crew members can register and log in to the website to publish and manage relevant information
User Registration: Users can register to become website members
Crew Registration: Crew members can register to become website members

2. Backstage functions
General user management: Administrators can manage the account information of registered users, such as adding, deleting, and modifying user information
Crew information management: Administrators can manage the account information of registered crews, such as adding, deleting, and modifying crew information
Administrator information management: Administrators can manage their own account information, such as changing passwords, viewing logs, etc.
News information management: Administrators can publish, edit, and delete news information
News column management: Administrators can add, delete, and modify news columns
Film and television information publishing management: Administrators can publish, edit, and delete information about movies and TV series
Comment information management: Administrators can view, review, and delete user comment information
Film and television ranking management: Administrators can adjust the ranking rules for movies and TV series
System maintenance: Administrators can perform basic system maintenance, such as backing up the database, updating the system, etc.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0246
CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `login_status` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `username` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `crew` (
  `crew_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `crew_information` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `crew_members` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `crew_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`crew_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `film_information` (
  `information_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `information_title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `information_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `publish_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`information_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment` (
  `film_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `comment_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`film_id`, `user_id`, `comment_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`film_id`) REFERENCES `film_information` (`information_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comment_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `film_ranking` (
  `ranking_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `film_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `ranking_position` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `update_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`ranking_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `film_ranking_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`film_id`) REFERENCES `film_information` (`information_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
